solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bishops after court pardoned thief

indicators.note: after places the bishops' word behind the court's word in the answer

parts.note: the bar is a court of law, or the barrier in one
abba is a title given to bishops in the Syriac and Coptic churches; here plural

explanation.surface: A thief walks free after court proceedings involving some bishops.
explanation.walkthrough: BARABBAS is the thief released instead of Jesus in the Gospels. ABBA as a bishop's title is a Chambers-dictionary sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Gospels the crowd chose Barabbas, a robber, to be released by Pilate instead of Jesus.

clue.text: Smack is a fishing vessel

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a two-masted boat used in herring fishing

explanation.walkthrough: A smack is also a fishing boat, so the surface reads as one definition of a boat; here it is a kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: Buss is an old word for a hearty kiss, and separately the name of a Dutch herring boat.

clue.text: Joy's bottom, any short hot pants would expose it

indicators.note: something short is missing its final part, so the word any loses its last letter
in a down clue, being at the bottom means coming last in the column

parts.note: any cut short
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
a synonym for great joy

explanation.surface: A cheeky remark about skimpy hot pants revealing someone called Joy's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: Pants is a verb in the definition, not underwear; Joy is a common noun, not a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Anhelation is a formal word for panting or breathlessness, which panting plainly displays.

clue.text: Opener out, cut with an edge

indicators.note: the opening letter is put out, so the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: trimmed means cut neatly

explanation.surface: Instructions for opening a tin: remove the opener and slice along the edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rimmed has a border or rim around it, that is, an edge.

clue.text: One penetrating large needle in small chassis

indicators.note: penetrating means going into, so the first piece is pushed inside the second

parts.note: a bodkin is a large blunt needle for threading tape
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A large needle pierces something inside a small chassis.
explanation.walkthrough: Chassis is slang for the human body, and the answer is an old diminutive, a little body.
explanation.definitionFit: Bodikin is an archaic diminutive of body, and chassis is jocular slang for a person's body or frame.

clue.text: Brass work at sustaining tuning note following endless bass beat

indicators.note: with no end, the word bass loses its final letter
to sustain is to hold up, so the brass-and-work pair holds the note within it
following means coming after, so the first part of the clue goes after the shortened bass

parts.note: bass without its last letter
both are slang for money
to do a subject is to work at it
an orchestra tunes to the note A

explanation.surface: A musical description of brass players holding a tuning note over a pounding bass line.
explanation.walkthrough: Every word here sounds musical, but brass is slang for money and beat is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To bastinado is to beat someone, especially on the soles of the feet, as a punishment.

clue.text: Walrus remains under stone

indicators.note: in a down clue, under puts one part below another in the column

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the weight
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: The remains of a walrus found beneath a rock.
explanation.walkthrough: Walrus is not the animal but a walrus moustache, droopy and thick.
explanation.definitionFit: Stash is informal for a moustache, and a walrus is a big drooping moustache.

clue.text: Name put forward in important part of Buddhist temple

indicators.note: the name's letter is moved further forward, which rearranges the order of the word's letters

parts.note: main means chief or important; its N is the name's letter

explanation.surface: Someone proposes a name for an important section of a Buddhist temple.
explanation.walkthrough: The N of MAIN moves one place forward, ahead of the I.
explanation.definitionFit: A mani is a Tibetan Buddhist prayer wall or stone inscribed with prayers, found at temples and shrines.

clue.text: Term for tub in front of mosque Iran constructed?

definitions.text: Term for tub in front of mosque Iran constructed?

indicators.note: something constructed is built up anew, so these letters are assembled in a fresh order
a term is an end, so only the final letter of the following word is kept

parts.note: first letter of mosque

indicators.note: in places the one letter inside the rearranged country

parts.note: the country's letters rearranged

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

parts.note: last letter of tub

explanation.surface: A query whether a particular word for a pulpit in front of an Iranian mosque was built there.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: tub is old slang for a pulpit, as in tub-thumper, and a minbar stands at the front of a mosque.
explanation.definitionFit: A minbar is the raised pulpit in a mosque from which the imam preaches, and tub is slang for a pulpit.

clue.text: Waffle with what's left of apples — cookers

indicators.note: with simply sets one piece beside the other
the leftmost part of a written word is its first letter

parts.note: the left end of apples
gas is idle talk, waffle

explanation.surface: A kitchen scene: waffles and leftover apples, then the cooking apples.
explanation.walkthrough: What's left of apples looks like leftovers; it is the left-hand letter. An Aga is a heavy British range cooker, a staple of country kitchens.
explanation.definitionFit: Aga is a brand of heat-storage range cooker, so Agas are cookers.

clue.text: Among alcoholic drinks mentioned, they have an edge

indicators.note: something mentioned is spoken, so the phrase is taken by its sound

parts.note: among is in, and ciders are alcoholic drinks

explanation.surface: A remark about people at a drinks party who have a sharp edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Insiders have privileged information, which gives them an advantage over everyone else.

clue.text: Out of date designation forming antibody stimulant

indicators.note: forming means shaping into something new, so the remaining letters are rearranged
out of means removed from, so the date letter is taken away

parts.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for date

explanation.surface: An obsolete name for something that triggers antibodies.
explanation.walkthrough: Out of date looks like obsolete; date is only the letter D, taken out.
explanation.definitionFit: An isoantigen is an antigen from one individual that provokes antibody production in another of the same species.

clue.text: Member boring second house is one?

definitions.text: Member boring second house is one?

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so this letter goes inside the house

parts.note: HO is the abbreviation for house
M is the abbreviation for member, as in MP

explanation.surface: Is the Member of Parliament who bores the second chamber a fool?
explanation.walkthrough: Boring is not tedious but drilling; the whole clue doubles as the definition, a tedious MP being a dolt.
explanation.definitionFit: Shmo is American slang for a stupid or contemptible person, which a boring Member arguably is.

clue.text: More than one goblet from Chinese resort sent back

parts.note: the Han are the majority Chinese people

indicators.note: something sent back goes the other way, so the resort is read from its end

parts.note: a spa is a health resort

explanation.surface: Several goblets returned from a holiday resort in China.
explanation.definitionFit: A hanap is an ornate medieval drinking cup or goblet, often with a lid.

clue.text: Nipper's toy potty is bent

indicators.note: potty means crazy, so the letters before it are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A child's toy potty has been bent out of shape.
explanation.walkthrough: Potty looks like the child's toilet; it is the scramble signal, meaning mad.
explanation.definitionFit: A bent is a natural inclination or tendency, which is what a propensity is.

clue.text: Model embraces Madame returning in tartan undergarment

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold within, so the model wraps round the other piece

parts.note: to model for an artist is to sit

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: Mme is the abbreviation of Madame

explanation.surface: A model hugging a French lady while dressed in tartan underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: Tartan signals a Scottish word.
explanation.definitionFit: Semmit is the Scots word for an undershirt or vest, and tartan stands for Scottish.

clue.text: Mongrel seizes cat to get excited

indicators.note: a mongrel is of mixed breed, so these letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A mongrel dog grabs a cat and gets worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: Mongrel reads as the dog doing the seizing, but it signals a mix.
explanation.definitionFit: To ecstasize is to go into ecstasy, to become wildly excited or enraptured.

clue.text: Joy has Knight in old card game

indicators.note: has means is followed by, attaching the knight after the joy

parts.note: glee is joy
K is the chess abbreviation for knight

explanation.surface: A joyful knight playing an old card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Gleek was a three-handed card game popular in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

clue.text: In Aberdeen, small drilling benefits pipework

indicators.note: drilling means boring into, so the small word goes inside the other
Aberdeen is in Scotland, so the next word is wanted in its Scots form

parts.note: gains are benefits
sma' is Scots for small

explanation.surface: In Aberdeen, a small-scale drilling operation brings benefits to the pipeline network.
explanation.definitionFit: Gas mains are the large pipes that carry the gas supply, a kind of pipework.

clue.text: Bach I do fancy for "The glory is departed"

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or ornamental, so these letters are dressed up in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone declares a fondness for Bach while lamenting lost glory.
explanation.definitionFit: In 1 Samuel, Ichabod is the child's name, interpreted as meaning the glory has departed from Israel.

clue.text: Mistake with spades in long suit

indicators.note: in places this pair inside the long word

parts.note: to pine is to long for

indicators.note: with puts the spades sign beside the mistake

parts.note: S is the card abbreviation for spades
a trip is a slip or mistake

explanation.surface: A card-player's error: misjudging spades while holding a long suit.
explanation.walkthrough: Long suit is bridge talk, but long is the verb and suit is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinstripe is a suit made of cloth with thin vertical stripes, the City banker's uniform.

clue.text: What ultimately supports French church is timber beam

indicators.note: in a down clue, what supports sits underneath

parts.note: temple is the French word for a Protestant church

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter of the word is kept

parts.note: last letter of what

explanation.surface: A question about what holds up a church in France, answered by a wooden beam.
explanation.definitionFit: A templet is a short timber or stone beam placed in a wall to spread the load of a girder or joist.

clue.text: Salts provided by American navy repeatedly in eg Virginia and Florida

indicators.note: in places the short letters inside the larger word

parts.note: these are two US states

indicators.note: repeatedly means the abbreviation for navy is used twice in a row

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for American
N for navy, twice

explanation.surface: Mineral salts supplied by the US Navy at bases in Virginia and Florida.
explanation.definitionFit: Stannates are salts of stannic acid, compounds containing tin and oxygen.

clue.text: Shellfish coming from Cannes? Right for number out to lunch

indicators.note: out to lunch means crazy, so the letters are scrambled
one letter stands in for another, the abbreviation for right replacing the abbreviation for number

parts.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right
N is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: Seafood from Cannes, ordered by a diner going out for lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the two Ns in CANNES becomes R before the scramble.
explanation.definitionFit: Nacre is mother-of-pearl, and the word is also used for the pearl-bearing shellfish that produce it.

clue.text: Run into huge beast and you'll get gloomy

indicators.note: into means going inside, so the letter is placed within the beast

parts.note: the moose is a very large deer
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Bumping into an enormous animal would make anyone downcast.
explanation.walkthrough: Run into reads as colliding; run is a letter that goes into the beast.
explanation.definitionFit: Morose means sullen and gloomy in mood.

clue.text: Girl missing in action outside border

indicators.note: outside means surrounding, so the military phrase wraps round the border

parts.note: MIA is the military abbreviation
a rand is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A girl has gone missing in action somewhere beyond the border.
explanation.definitionFit: Miranda is a girl's name, notably the heroine of The Tempest.

clue.text: Pointer once part of the One-Eleven

indicators.note: part of means the answer is a piece taken from the words that follow

parts.note: found across the hyphenated name

explanation.surface: A former pointer that was a component of the BAC One-Eleven airliner.
explanation.walkthrough: The One-Eleven was a British jet airliner, so a pointer suggests a cockpit instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Neele is an obsolete spelling of needle, and a needle points, as on a dial.

clue.text: Months and months investing in advance

indicators.note: investing means clothing or wrapping, so the short abbreviation wraps round the other piece

parts.note: MOS is the abbreviation for months
on can mean ahead or forward, as in further on

explanation.surface: A financier's line about months of investing money up front.
explanation.definitionFit: Moon is a poetic word for a month, the time the moon takes to go through its phases.

clue.text: No veteran leading Italian soccer team

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a juvenile lead, the actor playing young leading parts
second meaning: the nickname of Juventus of Turin

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a team fielding no veterans, but it splits into two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A juve is short for juvenile lead in theatre, a young rather than veteran performer, and Juve is Juventus's nickname.

clue.text: Press about on time for old-style spread

indicators.note: on puts the time after the reshuffled press
about means turned around, so the letters are moved round

parts.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An instruction on pressing an old-fashioned spread on time.
explanation.definitionFit: Sperst is a Spenserian form meaning dispersed or scattered, an old past participle of spread out.

clue.text: Nice street below front on the right

indicators.note: in a down clue, below puts the street underneath
the front of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of the
rue is French for street, and Nice is in France

explanation.surface: A street in Nice running beneath the seafront on the right-hand side.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice is the French city, not the adjective; its streets are rues.
explanation.definitionFit: True can mean right or correct, as in a true statement.

clue.text: Hardened and wronged, Jay's for retirement

indicators.note: a letter due for retirement leaves, so it is removed from the word

parts.note: injured means wronged
jay is the spelling of the letter J

explanation.surface: Someone toughened and wronged, with a man called Jay retiring.
explanation.walkthrough: Jay is the letter's name spelt out, not a person or a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Inured means accustomed to hardship and so hardened against it.

clue.text: Dormouse seen in river no end of trouble

indicators.note: no means without, so that letter is taken away from the river

parts.note: the Loire is France's longest river

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: last letter of trouble

explanation.surface: A dormouse spotted in a river, causing no end of trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: No end of trouble looks like a lot of bother; it means without the last letter of trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: The loir is the fat or edible dormouse of Europe.

clue.text: Writers Bob, Ron and Eve somehow inspiring Elizabeth

indicators.note: inspiring literally means breathing in, so the jumble takes the name inside
somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are arranged anyhow

parts.note: a bob is a shilling, abbreviated S; old British money
taken as written
taken as written
Liz is short for Elizabeth

explanation.surface: Three writers named Bob, Ron and Eve take inspiration from a woman called Elizabeth.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob is not a name but old British slang for a shilling, written S.
explanation.definitionFit: Novelizers are writers who turn a story, often a film, into a novel.

clue.text: Strains apparent in society? Indeed

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for society
yes and indeed both affirm

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether tensions are visible in society, and answers yes.
explanation.walkthrough: Strains suggests tensions, but it is the verb meaning to sieve.
explanation.definitionFit: Sye is a dialect word meaning to strain or sieve liquid, so syes means strains.

clue.text: At close quarters as one sleuth faces another

parts.note: a private eye is a detective
facing, toe to toe
a second sleuth

explanation.surface: Two detectives confront each other face to face.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye to eye means face to face, physically very close as well as in agreement.
